gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's own 140W 4-Port charger (A2697) costs $89.99 on anker.com today, the same price as the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-Port. It has a display, two 140 W USB-C ports and a USB-C cable in the box, so a shopper who wants Anker doesn't have to pay $149.99 for the Prime 160W.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides (cited), both Notebookcheck pieces (cited news, top-result review) and our own page. Itechguides prices only UGREEN models: the 4-port at $119.99, the 5-port at $64.99, the Nexode X at $119.99, the 100W at $42.99 and the Air 65W at $24.99. It gives no Anker price at all. The Notebookcheck news piece lists only the UGREEN 160W at $89.99, the Anker Prime 160W at $149.99 and a UGREEN 100W 5-port at $69.99. Our page lists the Prime 67W and Prime 100W but not the A2697. None of them name the A2697 or a UGREEN bundle that includes a 240 W cable, and every ChatGPT answer frames the choice as UGREEN at $90 against Anker at $150.
decides: It confirms UGREEN on price but changes the Anker side of the answer. At $89.99, a shopper who prefers Anker or wants a cable in the box can buy the A2697 for the UGREEN's price. They give up 20 W of total output (140 W, or 134 W with four devices) and a fifth port. The Prime 160W's $60 premium then pays only for the smaller 65 × 52 × 35 mm, 220 g body, a third full-power USB-C port and the app. The UGREEN 160W + 240 W cable bundle at $71.60 also undercuts the bare UGREEN charger at $89.99 and adds the cable a 140 W laptop needs. ChatGPT showed that bundle as the 'older 4-port version', but I could not confirm which charger it contains.
